secp256k1 discrete logarithm

Uniform x in the prime-order subgroup; fixed standard generator P. Given Q = [x]P, return x.

BLS12-381 pairing inversion

Fixed standard G2 generator Q₀. Given uniform z in GT, return P in G1 satisfying e(P, Q₀) = z.

Acceptance means a supported claim with no confirmed fatal flaw after AI review. It is not mathematical proof. Signed reviews, scores and previous attempts are preserved in the public evidence archive.

Two problems.
One clear metric.

Find algorithms that need less total computation to solve these problems on their full production parameters.

The score is log₂(total computation) in fixed target-group-operation equivalents. Lower is better. Success must be at least 39% over uniformly random challenges.

Preprocessing, failed attempts and work across all processors count. Memory is reported separately. Explain the complete cost calculation in the written argument.

How CurveSmash works

Choose a target and propose an algorithm that solves it with less total computation. Both targets use their full production parameters.

  1. Describe the attack. Specify the algorithm, justify its success probability and account for all its work.
  2. Submit the evidence. Include the written argument and any declared experiments or certificates.
  3. Review, then promotion. Four AI reviews examine the claim. Fatal objections receive defense and adjudication. An improving result still needs organizer approval before Yukon promotion.

A concrete, supported claim with no confirmed fatal flaw receives its submitted computation bound as the score. Remaining uncertainty is published. This follows HashSmash’s exploratory standard.

Read the participant guide

Review process

Four separate initial calls review the same frozen evidence. They currently use the same model, openai/gpt-5.6-sol.

Evaluability
Is the submission concrete and supported enough to assess?
Cryptanalysis
Does the attack solve the exact target, with the claimed success probability?
Cost
Does the written calculation cover all computation and resources?
Experiments
Do the measurements support the claims made from them?

Fatal objections receive a defense and adjudication. Confirmed flaws prevent scoring. Review acceptance is an exploratory finding, not a proof or human peer review.
